title: 1953 AHSME Problem 27
statement: The radius of the first circle is \(1\) inch, that of the second \(\dfrac12\) inch, that of the third \(\dfrac14\) inch and so on indefinitely. The sum of the areas of the circles is:

solutions.text:
The areas are \[ \pi,\ \frac{\pi}{4},\ \frac{\pi}{16},\ldots \] Therefore their sum is \[ \frac{\pi}{1-\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{4\pi}{3}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Squaring each radius changes the common ratio
The areas form a geometric series with first term \(\pi\) and ratio \(\frac{1}{4}\)
